summary: Mauke Airport (MUK) is a small domestic airstrip serving Mauke Island, one of the remote outer islands of the Cook Islands in the South Pacific. The airport provides essential air connectivity to Rarotonga, the main island, for local residents and a small number of adventurous visitors drawn to Mauke's volcanic landscapes, limestone caves, and traditional Polynesian culture. It features a single short runway suited to small turboprop aircraft operating inter-island flights.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines fly to Mauke Airport?
A: Air Rarotonga operates scheduled domestic flights between Rarotonga and Mauke, typically using small Saab or BN Islander aircraft suitable for the short runway.

Q: How long is the flight from Rarotonga to Mauke?
A: The flight from Rarotonga to Mauke generally takes around 50 to 60 minutes, depending on weather and routing.

Q: Is Mauke Airport used for international flights?
A: No, Mauke Airport is a domestic facility only. All international travelers must enter through Rarotonga International Airport before connecting onward.

Q: Are there airport facilities at Mauke?
A: Facilities are minimal, reflecting the airport's small size. There is no jet bridge, limited terminal space, and services are basic — travelers should arrive prepared.
transport_tips: Getting from Mauke Airport to your accommodation typically requires arranging a rental car or transfer in advance, as taxi services are very limited on the island. The airport is located on the western side of Mauke, within a short drive of Omoa, the main settlement. Some guesthouses and lodges offer airport pickup when bookings are made in advance.
local_tip: Bring a light jacket and rain gear — Mauke is noticeably wetter and cooler than Rarotonga due to its elevated volcanic terrain, and showers can arrive quickly even during the dry season.
